# agent_type: # agent_type is what Claude Code puts in the hook input: redline:redline-<role> for the plugin's
# agents, redline-<role> for a copy installed into .claude/agents/, anything else for other agents,
# and - for none (the main session). expected is allow, deny, or inert (exit 0, no output: not a
# Redline role). REPO/ is the repository root, PLUGIN/ the plugin root; \n is expanded.
# A line `# @cwd PLUGIN` sends the rows after it from the plugin's checkout as the repository (Redline
# reviewing itself); `# @cwd REPO` (the default) sends them from the repository the test runs in.

command or path: git commit -m "redline: R1-1 reject an empty order reference (#42)"
git commit -m "redline: R1-8 point the git tip in .claude/commands/agent-os/shape-spec.md at CLAUDE.md (#42)"
git commit -m "redline: R1-8 tidy CLAUDE.md as Claude suggested (#42)"
git commit -m "redline: R1-8 fix per Anthropic docs (#42)"
grep -l x app | xargs grep -n y
git -C REPO/ log --oneline -3 && git -C REPO/ status --porcelain
php artisan test --compact tests/Feature/Api/OrderControllerTest.php 2>&1 | python3 -c "import sys; print(sys.stdin.read()[-200:])"
git commit -m 'redline: R1-2 state the rounding rule in the docblock (#42)'
grep -n x#y app ; git push --force origin main

# agent_type: # Not a Redline role: the guard does nothing, whatever the command.
# A Redline-shaped agent_type whose role is not in the table is refused.
# A copy installed into .claude/agents/ is guarded the same way.
# The plugin's own directory and the per-repo config are Redline's own files.
# In a repository that is not the plugin, a file by one of the plugin's names is ordinary content.
# Another spelling of a protected path is the same file on a case-insensitive volume (#5, R1-4).
# redline-gh.sh runs only from the plugin; a copy where the tool tier used to live is not it.
# Step 13: the saved preferences file (.claude/redline.local.json) is one of Redline's own files,
# and the preferences script is the skill's, never a role's. The main session, which runs the
# skill, is not a Redline role, so the guard is inert for it. The gate stamp script (#6) is the
# skill's in the same way: no role runs it, and a role can never restamp checks.sh.

command or path: PLUGIN/scripts/redline-prefs.sh save REPO/ --interrupt autopilot --revise opus --max-rounds 3 --scope all

# agent_type: # The setup script (#6, second half) is the skill's in the same way: no role runs any of its
# subcommands, and .claude/redline/checks.json, the source checks.sh is generated from, is one of
# Redline's own files like checks.sh, so no role may write it either.
# Step 14: Finish commits the run record. The GitHub agent lists the record's uncommitted files
# with git status, stages them by name (agent-os/specs/ only, its write prefix), commits with the
# redline: prefix and pushes. Read-only git is all it gains for reading: no file tools.

command or path: git -C REPO/ commit -m "redline: record the run's replies, reviews and handoff for PR #42 (#42)"
git -C REPO/ commit -a -m "redline: record the run"
git -C REPO/ commit --amend -m "redline: record the run"
git -C REPO/ commit -m "redline: record the run\n\nCo-Authored-By: someone"

# agent_type: # The repository is the plugin: Redline loaded in place from its own checkout, reviewing itself
# (issue #4). The plugin's source is repository content under the roles' usual prefixes; .claude/'s
# Redline files stay refused, and so do the guard and the hook that registers it, for every role.

command or path: git commit -m "redline: R1-1 resolve the plugin root once (#4)"
